paper.title_en: Nonperturbative renormalization of Haldane pseudopotentials from the exact two-electron spectrum
paper.abstract_en: We investigate how exact two-electron energies and radial wavefunctions can improve many-electron descriptions of Landau-level (LL) mixing. Renormalized pseudopotentials are defined from the lowest interacting relative-motion branch in each lowest-LL angular-momentum channel. They include changes in Coulomb and magnetic kinetic expectation values nonperturbatively and recover the leading two-body perturbative correction. Matched three- and four-electron benchmarks show that the scalar renormalized model improves lowest fixed-sector energies and first fixed-sector spacings over conventional lowest-LL projection, although the tested perturbative models give more accurate lowest energies. Retaining the same second-order induced three-body term while replacing the perturbative two-body input by the renormalized pseudopotentials yields a hybrid with smaller absolute lowest-energy errors throughout the sampled coupling range. At the Coulomb-to-cyclotron energy ratio $γ_B=3.5$, the errors decrease by approximately $58\%$ and $57\%$ for three and four electrons, respectively, relative to the tail-completed two-plus-three-body perturbative comparator. At the same coupling, complementary antisymmetric multi-LL variational states built from the pair radial amplitudes recover $99.41\%$ and $99.11\%$ of the matched finite-cutoff LL-mixing energy lowering for five and six electrons, outperforming equal-rank first-order-pair controls. These results establish pair energies and radial structure as complementary, quantitatively useful inputs for many-electron treatments of LL mixing.
